{{Short description|Dutch physicist}}
[[File:Albert van den Berg.jpg|thumb|right|Albert van den Berg]]
'''Albert van den Berg''' (born 20 September 1957) is a Dutch physicist who works on [[nanotechnology]]-miniaturization in physics, chemistry, biology and biotechnology ([[nanofluidics]], [[nanosensor]]s, ''Lab on a chip'' (LOC), Organ on Chip (OoC)).

Van den Berg was born in [[Zaandam]].  In 1988 he earned his PhD at the [[University of Twente]] with a thesis on chemically modified [[Ion sensitive field effect transistor|ISFET]]s. Then until 1993 he worked at the ''Centre Suisse d'Electronique et de Microtechnique'' (CSEM) in [[Neuchâtel]] and the ''Institut de microtechnique'' (IMT) at the [[University of Neuchâtel]]. During this time he worked mainly on miniaturized chemical sensors. From 1993 to 1999 he was director of research for Micro Total Analysis Systems (<math>\mu</math>TAS, i.e. miniaturized systems for chemical analysis) and Miniaturized Chemical Systems (MiCS) at the Institute for Nanotechnology (MESA<sup>+</sup>) at the University of Twente.<ref>[http://www.utwente.nl/mesaplus/scientists/ MESA<sup>+</sup>, Institute for Nanotechnology, U. of Twente]</ref> In 1998 he had a part-time professorship and from 2000 a full professorship. In 2003 he became head of nanofluidics within the Dutch national nanotechnology program ([[NanoNed]]). Van den Berg has co-authored over 500 scientific publications ([[h-index|H]]=63) and over 10 patents. He is or has been involved with 10 spin-off companies.<ref>[http://www.utwente.nl/ewi/bios/People/scientificstaff/Berg/Biography%20short/ Brief bio from U. of Twente]</ref> He is currently one of two co-directors of the MESA+ Institute at the University of Twente.

In 2002 he won the Simon Stevin Master Award of the Dutch Society of Science and Engineering. In 2009 he won the [[Spinoza Prize]],<ref>[http://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/programmes/spinoza+prize/spinoza+laureates/overview+in+alphabetical+order/albert+van+den+berg Prof. Albert van den Berg, NWO Netherlands website]</ref> the most prestigious Dutch science prize. As there was no fourth Spinoza Prize awarded in 2009, Van den Berg and his co-winners [[Michel Ferrari]] and [[Marten Scheffer]] asked the NWO to reward them the remaining prize money, which they would spend on a collaborative research effort.<ref>{{cite news|author1=Jannetje Koelewijn |author2=Jop de Vrieze |url=http://vorige.nrc.nl/wetenschap/article2289021.ece/Knappe_koppen_zonder_hoofdpijn |title=Knappe koppen zonder hoofdpijn |language=Dutch |newspaper=[[NRC Handelsblad]] |date=4 July 2009 |access-date=1 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151120155325/http://vorige.nrc.nl/wetenschap/article2289021.ece/Knappe_koppen_zonder_hoofdpijn |archive-date=20 November 2015 }}</ref> Their efforts culminated in a research paper on [[migraine]] published in ''[[PLOS ONE]]'' in 2013.<ref>{{Cite journal|author1=Marten Scheffer |author2=Albert van den Berg |author3=Michel D. Ferrari |title=Migraine Strikes as Neuronal Excitability Reaches a Tipping Point |volume=8 |issue=8 |article-number=e72514 |journal=[[PLOS ONE]] |date=29 August 2013 |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0072514 |pmid=24009688 |pmc=3757026|bibcode=2013PLoSO...872514S |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=Paul de Kuyper |url=http://www.utnieuws.nl/nieuws/59163/Eerste_migrainepublicatie_drie_Spinozawinnaars |title=Eerste migraine-publicatie drie Spinoza-winnaars |language=Dutch |publisher=UT Nieuws |date=4 September 2013 |access-date=2 August 2015 |archive-date=22 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160822040444/http://www.utnieuws.nl/nieuws/59163/Eerste_migrainepublicatie_drie_Spinozawinnaars |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=nwomigraine>{{cite web|url=http://www.nwo.nl/en/news-and-events/news/2013/migraine-consequence-of-critical-tipping-point-in-neural-network.html |title=Migraine consequence of critical tipping point in neural network |publisher=Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research |date=4 September 2013 |access-date=2 August 2015}}</ref> The paper claimed that a critical tipping point of neurons started a migraine attack.<ref name=nwomigraine/>

He is a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] since 2008, and its council 2011–2016.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.utwente.nl/ewi/bios/People/scientificstaff/Berg/biography%20long/ |title=Bio from ''Lab on a Chip'' Research group at the University of Twente |access-date=2014-02-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221232746/http://www.utwente.nl/ewi/bios/People/scientificstaff/Berg/biography%20long/ |archive-date=2014-02-21 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://iscoms.com/programme/keynote-lectures/a-v-d-berg/ |title=Prof. Albert van den Berg PhD – ISCOMS '14 |access-date=2014-02-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140203200620/http://iscoms.com/programme/keynote-lectures/a-v-d-berg/ |archive-date=2014-02-03 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/7953 |title=Albert van den Berg |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |access-date=17 July 2015}}</ref>

==Works==
*Editor with R. Edwin Oosterbroek: ''Lab-on-a-chip: miniaturized systems for (bio)chemical analysis and synthesis'', Elsevier 2003
*Editor with Helene Andersson: ''Lab on Chip for Cellomics. Micro - and Nanotechnologies for Life Science'', Kluwer/Springer Verlag 2007
*Editor with Séverine Le Gac: ''Miniaturization and Mass Spectroscopy'', Royal Society of Chemistry Publishing 2009
*Editor of conference volumes on Micro Total Analysis Systems, e.g. for the Workshops in 1994, 1998, 2000
